Summary: CM01: To log a complaint from my teller workstation
Description: As a branch employee, I want to log a complaint from my teller workstation, so that I stop using paper forms. (Traces to FR01, BR01)
Acceptance Criteria: Screen opens from customer profile in under 3 seconds; customer and channel pre filled; save creates complaint ID.

Summary: CM02: To turn a complaint email into a CRM record in one click
Description: As a complaints specialist, I want to turn a complaint email into a CRM record in one click, so that I stop re keying emails. (Traces to FR02, BR01)
Acceptance Criteria: Original email attached; sender matched to customer where possible; received date set to email date.

Summary: CM03: To create a complaint from a social media message
Description: As a digital team member, I want to create a complaint from a social media message, so that it enters the same process as every other complaint. (Traces to FR03, BR01)
Acceptance Criteria: Post link and screenshot stored; received date set to first seen date.

Summary: CM04: To attach a scanned letter when logging it
Description: As a complaints specialist, I want to attach a scanned letter when logging it, so that the original is kept with the record. (Traces to FR04, BR01)
Acceptance Criteria: PDF or image up to 20 MB attached; received date set to date stamped on arrival.

Summary: CM05: The received date recorded separately from the logged date
Description: As a compliance officer, I want the received date recorded separately from the logged date, so that the 56 day clock is measured correctly. (Traces to FR05, BR02)
Acceptance Criteria: Field mandatory; future dates blocked; received date later than logged date blocked with message.

Summary: CM06: To be told quickly that my complaint was received
Description: As a customer, I want to be told quickly that my complaint was received, so that I know I have been heard. (Traces to FR06, BR03)
Acceptance Criteria: Sent within 1 business day of logging; includes complaint ID and next steps; logged on the record.

Summary: CM07: Updates when my complaint moves forward
Description: As a customer, I want updates when my complaint moves forward, so that I do not have to chase anyone. (Traces to FR07, BR03)
Acceptance Criteria: Update sent on escalation and on final response; logged on the record.

Summary: CM08: The due date calculated for me
Description: As a complaints specialist, I want the due date calculated for me, so that I never miscount the deadline. (Traces to FR08, BR04)
Acceptance Criteria: Due date equals received date plus 56 days; recalculated if received date is corrected, with audit entry.

Summary: CM09: Warnings before a complaint reaches day 56
Description: As a complaints specialist, I want warnings before a complaint reaches day 56, so that I can act in time. (Traces to FR09, BR04)
Acceptance Criteria: Alerts generated on the correct days for open complaints only; shown in CRM and by email.

Summary: CM10: A dashboard of open complaints by age
Description: As a complaints manager, I want a dashboard of open complaints by age, so that I can rebalance work before deadlines are missed. (Traces to FR10, BR04)
Acceptance Criteria: Age bands 0 to 29, 30 to 44, 45 to 49, 50 to 56, over 56; filters by owner and category; refreshed hourly.

Summary: CM11: A delay notice template with OBSI information
Description: As a complaints specialist, I want a delay notice template with OBSI information, so that customers get the information they are entitled to. (Traces to FR11, BR05)
Acceptance Criteria: Template in English and French; reason field mandatory; date sent logged.

Summary: CM12: To be told if a complaint is about to breach with no notice sent
Description: As a complaints manager, I want to be told if a complaint is about to breach with no notice sent, so that nothing slips through. (Traces to FR12, BR05)
Acceptance Criteria: Escalation at day 55 only when both are missing; manager notified in CRM and by email.

Summary: CM13: To assign tasks to other teams inside the CRM
Description: As a complaints specialist, I want to assign tasks to other teams inside the CRM, so that hand offs are tracked, not lost in email. (Traces to FR13, BR06)
Acceptance Criteria: Task has owner, due date and status; owner notified; overdue tasks highlighted.

Summary: CM14: To mark that I am waiting on a card network
Description: As a fraud and disputes specialist, I want to mark that I am waiting on a card network, so that everyone sees why the case is paused. (Traces to FR14, BR06)
Acceptance Criteria: Status available; expected date mandatory; visible on dashboard.

Summary: CM15: Fraud complaints routed straight to my queue
Description: As a fraud and disputes specialist, I want fraud complaints routed straight to my queue, so that they are handled by the right people quickly. (Traces to FR15, BR07)
Acceptance Criteria: Routing by category; priority set to High; other categories go to Complaints Office queue.

Summary: CM16: To see if this complaint is already logged
Description: As a frontline employee, I want to see if this complaint is already logged, so that we do not investigate the same issue twice. (Traces to FR16, BR08)
Acceptance Criteria: Matches shown before save; employee can link or confirm new; decision logged.

Summary: CM17: Every closed complaint to have an outcome and root cause
Description: As a compliance officer, I want every closed complaint to have an outcome and root cause, so that trend data is complete. (Traces to FR17, BR09)
Acceptance Criteria: Close button disabled until both selected; free text not accepted as root cause.

Summary: CM18: To control the root cause list
Description: As a complaints manager, I want to control the root cause list, so that categories stay consistent. (Traces to FR18, BR09)
Acceptance Criteria: Only manager role can add, edit or retire values; changes logged.

Summary: CM19: A monthly view of complaint root causes
Description: As a product owner, I want a monthly view of complaint root causes, so that I can fix problems at the source. (Traces to FR19, BR10)
Acceptance Criteria: Dashboard by month; drill down; Excel export; available to product owner role.

Summary: CM20: The complaint definition on screen when I log
Description: As a branch employee, I want the complaint definition on screen when I log, so that I know when a concern must be recorded. (Traces to FR20, BR11)
Acceptance Criteria: Definition shown; help link to procedure; in English and French.

Summary: CM21: A full, unalterable history of each complaint
Description: As a internal auditor, I want a full, unalterable history of each complaint, so that I can verify how it was handled. (Traces to FR21, BR12)
Acceptance Criteria: Every create, edit, status change and communication logged with user and time; no user can edit or delete entries.

Summary: CM22: A complaint report for any period
Description: As a compliance officer, I want a complaint report for any period, so that regulatory and board reporting is accurate and fast. (Traces to FR22, BR12)
Acceptance Criteria: Report by date range; matches underlying records; export to Excel.

Summary: CM23: Communications in my official language
Description: As a customer, I want communications in my official language, so that I fully understand them. (Traces to FR23, BR03)
Acceptance Criteria: Every template available in both languages; language follows customer preference.

Summary: CM24: To record and close a complaint I resolved on the spot
Description: As a branch employee, I want to record and close a complaint I resolved on the spot, so that resolved complaints are still on record. (Traces to FR24, BR01)
Acceptance Criteria: Resolved at first contact option; outcome and root cause required; closes immediately.
